title: Prebuilt addNoteHandler constant removed
detail: `addNoteHandler` is no longer exported from the notes-history feature. It was a default-access copy of the factory and nothing registered it; the feature builds its handler with `createAddNoteHandler`.
migration: Replace `addNoteHandler` with `createAddNoteHandler(access, entryExecutor)`, or mount `createNotesHistoryFeature({ parents })`, which registers the handler.

title: The deprecated notesHistoryFeature constant is removed
detail: notesHistoryFeature was kept next to createNotesHistoryFeature() for one release. Mount the feature by calling createNotesHistoryFeature().
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It replaces notesHistoryFeature with createNotesHistoryFeature().

title: forget-subject shreds note bodies even when the host entity has anonymize or blockDelete retention
notes-history adds a composite index on (tenantId, entityType, entityId) for note entries, so the schema-drift check fails until the app regenerates
detail:
Review batch H2: framework parts of consumer-app findings.
- `file-derivatives`: the `isPublic` predicate args carry `fileRefId`, so a predicate can reject a client-spoofed FileRef that claims another entity's `entityId`/`fieldName`.
- `sessions`: `createSessionsFeature({ adminAccess: "systemAdmin" })` narrows the admin list/detail queries and both admin screens together (default `"admin"`, unchanged).
- `user-profile`: `change-email` is open to every signed-in user (`openToAll`), so a tenant member whose only role is `TenantAdmin` can change their own email; the handler still re-checks the password.
- `notes-history`: composite index on `(tenantId, entityType, entityId)` for note entries. Apps run `kumiko-schema generate` after the bump.
- guards: `// kumiko-lint-ignore a,b reason` suppresses several guards on one line (`lineHasIgnoreTag`); `primitives-discipline` and `no-custom-primitives` honour it.
- dev-server: `kumiko-build --check` verifies `.kumiko/` is current without writing (exit 1 on drift); `runCodegen` takes `checkOnly`.
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` in apps that mount notes-history and commit the generated migration.

title: read_note_mentions gets a tenant, subject index
migration: Run `kumiko schema generate`; it emits an in-place CREATE INDEX with no DROP and no rebuild.

title: add-note rejects mentions of non-members; mention export lists mentioning notes
migration: No action needed unless a client mentions user ids that are not members of the tenant; those writes now fail validation.

title: NotesSection no longer wraps its own "new note" / "history" blocks in a Card (fw#3234)
detail: As an extension section (its documented usage: `component: { react: { __component: NOTES_SECTION_EXTENSION_NAME } }`), NotesSection was already mounted inside the host's own section frame — its two internal Cards doubled the border/padding there. Both blocks now use a plain container with a `Heading variant="section"` sub-header instead.
migration: A standalone `<NotesSection entityName={...} entityId={id} />` mount (outside a screen-schema extension section) now renders both blocks without their own card chrome — wrap it in a `Section`/`Card` if the standalone mount needs one.

title: add-note now always verifies entityType/entityId against the parent entity's own read path
migration: entityType must now name an entity registered in the same app (via r.entity(...) or a bundled feature), and the caller must be able to see the target row through that entity's own read path. Any consumer that called add-note with an entityType that is NOT a registered entity name, or with an entityId the caller could not otherwise read, will now get a not_found error instead of a successful write — register the parent entity (and, if it needs row-level ownership, its `access.read` rule) before upgrading.

title: note-entry gains authorName, stamped at write time
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply — the migration adds `read_note_entries.authorName`. No backfill: existing rows read null and show the placeholder, same as before this change from the user's point of view.
